lessons.title: Iolra -í
lessons.rule: For a fourth-declension noun ending in -a or -ín, add -í in the plural (mála, málaí; sicín, sicíní); for one ending in -e, change the -e to -í (ceapaire, ceapairí).
steps: Mála ends in -a, so add -í.
The plural is málaí.
Write it after na: Fág na málaí ag an doras, le do thoil.

example.prompt: Fág na (mála) ag an doras, le do thoil.
example.answer: Fág na málaí ag an doras, le do thoil.

more.answer: Cheannaigh mé na ceapairí sa siopa.

items.prompt: Scríobh mé na (nóta) ar an fhón.
items.answer: Scríobh mé na nótaí ar an fhón.
Chaill mé na cártaí sa bhus.

items.prompt: Scríobh mé na (aiste) ar an ríomhaire glúine.
items.answer: Scríobh mé na haistí ar an ríomhaire glúine.
Glanann siad na seomraí achan Satharn.

lessons.title: Iolra -the agus -te
lessons.rule: A noun ending in -aí changes it to -aithe in the plural (tacsaí, tacsaithe), and some nouns ending in -e change it to -te (tine, tinte).
steps: Tacsaí ends in -aí.
Change -aí to -aithe: tacsaithe.
Write it after na: Tháinig na tacsaithe chuig an scoil.

example.answer: Tháinig na tacsaithe chuig an scoil.

more.prompt: Las siad na (tine) ar an trá.
more.answer: Las siad na tinte ar an trá.

items.answer: An gcuimhin leat na sloinnte sin?

lessons.title: Iolra -anna
lessons.rule: Many nouns ending in a vowel add -nna in the plural (lao, laonna; cú, cúnna; trá, tránna), and short words ending in a consonant add -anna (bus, busanna; pas, pasanna).
steps: Lao ends in a vowel, so add -nna.
The plural is laonna.
Write it after na: Chonaic mé na laonna ar an fheirm.

example.prompt: Chonaic mé na (lao) ar an fheirm.
example.answer: Chonaic mé na laonna ar an fheirm.

more.answer: Bhí na busanna mall ar maidin.

lessons.hint: Vowel at the end: add -nna; consonant: add -anna.

items.prompt: Rinne mé na (glao) ar an fhón.
items.answer: Rinne mé na glaonna ar an fhón.

items.prompt: D'ith muid na (cnó) ag an tine.
items.answer: D'ith muid na cnónna ag an tine.
Chaill siad na pasanna san aerfort.

lessons.title: An ginideach uatha: ainmfhocail fhirinscneacha
lessons.rule: In the fourth declension the noun itself does not change in the genitive singular: after an, just add séimhiú (an bus, uimhir an bhus), put t before s and a vowel (an tsicín), and leave vowels, d, t and st alone.
steps: The end of the noun does not change: bus.
Add séimhiú after an: an bhus.
Write the phrase: Uimhir an bhus.

lessons.title: An ginideach uatha: ainmfhocail bhaininscneacha
lessons.rule: For a feminine noun, change an to na and take off any séimhiú or t; put h before a vowel. The noun itself does not change: an aiste, fad na haiste; an tsaoire, deireadh na saoire.
steps: Aiste is feminine, so change an to na.
It begins with a vowel, so put h in front of it: na haiste.
Write the phrase: Fad na haiste.
lessons.hint: Feminine: na, no séimhiú, h before a vowel.

lessons.title: An ginideach iolra
lessons.rule: In the genitive plural keep the plural form and eclipse it after na (na cluichí, deireadh na gcluichí); put n- before a vowel, and leave l, m, n, r and s unchanged.
steps: Keep the plural form: cluichí.
Eclipse it after na: c becomes gc, na gcluichí.
Write the phrase: Deireadh na gcluichí.
lessons.hint: Plural form plus urú after na.

lessons.title: An ginideach i ndiaidh an ainm bhriathartha
lessons.rule: A noun after a verbal noun such as ag ól or ag íoc goes into the genitive: ag ól an chaife, ag íoc na táille, ag ithe na gceapairí.
steps: The noun follows ag ól, so it goes into the genitive.
Caife is masculine and its end does not change: add séimhiú after an, an chaife.
Write the phrase: Ag ól an chaife.
lessons.hint: After ag + verbal noun, use the genitive.
